decisions.reason: The downward pour direction does not change the platform height, footprint, supported cup size, or clearance purpose.
Spout pour direction does not alter the requirement that the dispensing path be removable and easy to clean.
The source changes spout orientation, while the valve mechanism, operator control, dispensing sequence, and controlled-flow requirements remain unchanged.
The downward pour direction does not change the required leak-free seal behavior.
The orientation change does not modify the requirement to prevent liquid from reaching the base or electrical components.
The source concerns consistency during dispensing and does not change whisk selection, whisk positioning, mixing quality, or frothing behavior.
Spout pour direction has no stated effect on electrical loads, power-supply capacity, controllers, or overload protection.
The spout orientation decision does not alter bowl capacity, depth, enclosure constraints, or other bowl geometry attributes.
The source does not change the placement or layout of speed, dispense, or master-power controls.
The spout's downward pour direction does not change placard text, position, duplication, or viewing orientation.
The source attributes the downward pour to drink consistency and does not establish a new splash-control constraint or mitigation.
The spout orientation decision does not alter any body, accent, support-base, or font color requirement.
